rationale: The workflow runs install/build/test across a three-version Node matrix with no job timeout bound. Historical CI runs complete in roughly 25 seconds, so representative successful-duration history exists, satisfying the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT precondition. The measured fork experiment batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT) kept all 3 runs successful while adding timeout-minutes: 5 and reduced median elapsed time 41s to 30s (26.8%). Applying the same minimal bound to this job prevents runaway consumption without removing any step, test, or matrix variant, so build and test coverage is preserved. The contraindication (valid slow runs exceed the limit) does not apply because normal runs (~25s) are far below 5 minutes. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is not applicable because dependency caching already exists via setup-node cache:pnpm, and P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is not applied because every Node-version matrix outcome is required for this library's CI.
